For a fixed fiber and old unit normal e, the new cutting plane is a graph over e-perpendicular because the perturbed continuous normal has positive dot product with e. Its cutting height is a smooth rational function of the perturbed coefficients, with uniform first-order expansion on the compact projection and at every fixed sampled base.

On each old line interval the retained length is a 1-Lipschitz function of the cutting height. Away from an old endpoint it is locally affine in the height, with slope minus one on proper line cuts and zero on saturated lines. For an arbitrary sequence of parameter increments the pointwise difference quotient of the linearization error tends to zero, and the uniform height bound dominates it on the finite projection. This proves the full Fréchet derivative, not just derivatives in fixed directions.

For a proper fiber trace, a boundary point in the section's relative interior would have a supporting normal perpendicular to the section plane, contradicting that the plane cuts the body interior. Thus line endpoints at the old height have a null footprint. At null supporting sections the footprint is already null, while strict saturation gives none. In dimension one the footprint is counted in dimension zero, so supporting endpoints are excluded and proper cuts differentiate by interval length.

At a section point the negative height derivative is exactly (a-dot·z+u-dot·x−b-dot)/‖u‖, and the orthogonal section coordinates preserve (d−1)-measure. The finite sum works for arbitrary real base labels and for a zero-dimensional base. The original smooth moment differentiation, signed chain rule, common fiber determinant and positive margin scaling are unchanged.
The original §1 (1)–(4) separates smooth hinge moments from the regular cap-mass derivative and treats positive-area supporting faces separately.

Because the continuous normal is nonzero, L=0 has zero d-volume in every fiber. Compact support gives a common dominating bound on all unit affine parameter directions. Pointwise derivatives and parameter-continuous coordinate gradients give the stated C¹ formulas for Ψ and T.

The ordinary chain rule gives the signed sum of coarea, captured mass and L-weighted captured mass, with no sign constraint on the cost partial derivatives. The absolute common fiber determinant and the positive margin rescaling give the two distinct stated scaling laws.

A support seam cannot be silently included. For K=[0,1] and margin x−1+t the closed cap mass is t for 0<t<1 and zero for −1<t<0, whereas both smooth hinge moments have derivative zero there. The d=1 coarea section at t=0 has H₀ mass one.
